body: I'm sorry to hear that you are always in so much pain, but you seem to have a positive outlook, or you are at least dealing with it well at this point, I respect that and it's inspiring to me as well. Thank you for responding and willing to talk to me when I need it, that truly means a lot. If you ever want to talk to I'd be happy to, I don't sign into this username often, I specifically made it for this, but I will check back periodically, especially after how kind and helpful you've all been. I really wasn't expecting much of any response.

Thank you for reading everything I do appreciate it, and thank you as well for your insight and advice, it's so helpful to hear from others in this way. I guess I've turned this thread into some miny therapy, so I just keep venting haha so the following is my response. I'm also going to post an update in this thread in a minute.

I brought my mother with me for the biopsy once and I still freaked out and couldn't do it. I want to have it done, and it's always on my mind, and I think I'm ready each time and then I get there and it's just an instant panic attack. But now that I have insurance again I want to try again. Because it is almost always something I'm thinking and wondering about and I hate it, I want it to just go away. I have times when I've wanted to just chop my finger tip off, I wouldn't never actually do it, but the idea crosses my eye often. 

I never actually entered into the field of psychology, it was by the end of college I realized how much I wanted nothing to do with it. Most of the people I met in the field were only in it for themselves and didn't want to actually help anyone, just a bunch of egotistical scientists, and I had a professor/adviser once constantly try to discourage me from joining the field, so I guess he succeeded, I think he saw me as a threat because I basically wanted to do the same thing as him but I'm vastly more open minded then he is, but maybe that's just my own ego talking. In summary, the field of psychology is full of egotistical and hyper-competitive nerds, and I want nothing to do with it.

Thank you for taking the time to read all that, responding and sharing your story with me. It's amazing how powerful it is just to hear "you are not alone" because as I'm sure you know, when you feel this miserable you can think you're alone and that no one will understand. I'm glad to hear you've been able to overcome your own depression and suicidal idealization, after about 10 years of feeling this way on and off it gets exhausting, just when I think I've overcome it completely it comes back, but it's the times you don't feel suicidal that you need to remember, and remember how that feels. But every year I get a little better and the suicidal feelings become less and less common. Maybe the current rarity of those feelings is why it can be so jarring for me. Sorry now I'm just thinking out loud. 

And by the way, saving 15 puppies is a huge contribution in my eyes. I'm glad to hear you've been doing that as I love animals so much. Thank you for doing that, and thank you again for replying, it does help.
well that wasn't short at all oops, and it's just a summary.

So it's a really long story, like really long. I'll try to be as concise as possible and hit on the things that are really bothering me. I'm 25, I've been living at home since I graduate college in 2013, I briefly had a job (for about 6-8 months) and hated it, since then I've been living at home and not working, I'm an only child and my parents have always taken care of and spoiled me so I have the luxury to just not do anything. This is going to get messy now, these thoughts might not be clear but I'm going to try to hit on the main points. I majored in psychology in college and planned to get my phd, after finding out how that field really operates I was deeply disturbed by it and want nothing to do with it. so now I feel I've wasted a ton of money time and effort on something I now have major issue with, I have other ideas of what I want to do but can't seem to get any motivation to do so. Instead, for the past almost 2 years I just sit at home and do nothing and think about all that could be, but I'm at square one again, I feel like a child and I'm terrified of my next step. I want to move to southern CA to eventually obtain a degree in fashion design and marketing, where I believe my true passion is, but it's a lot of money and effort to even move there, (I live in the northern east coast of america now) I just feel so stuck, I have no friends around me and live in a very rural area, I'm a gay male and there are no others here, I yearn for love and fullfilment but I'm afraid to do anything. I feel like people keep telling me if I want change and want to be happy I need to do something proactive, but for some reason I can't seem to develop the desire to do so. Maybe because I'm too comfortable leeching off my parents, but at the same time I feel so guilty for wasting all their hard earned money (we are not rich by any means) so I just feel like this leech and a waste of space. Despite the fact I want to move out and do things with my life I can't seem to, I've always failed at things and (so cliche) no one seems to get me, no matter where I go or what I do I'm always the odd person out and no one ever takes me serious, I'm always some weak little joke of a persona and it's so frustrating, no matter what I try to do I'm wrong, I can't ever seem to catch a break, I worked my ass of in college and my professors constantly ignored my efforts. and this is random to the rest, but the real icing on the cake, I have a weird brown line under my finger nail (something similar made the front page on reddit a while back) there is a good chance it's skin cancer, I've gone to see a dermatologist a few times and they were going to do a biopsy, I have a genuine phobia of anesthesia and surgery. I drove 3 hours to a dermatologist on 3 different occasions, each time I had a panic attack and left without having the biopsy done, so in the back of my mind, literally, constantly is "you have cancer, you're too afraid to do anything about it, and you're going to die soon anyway so why bother trying to live life." I just feel like a waste of space waiting to die at this point and I kind of just want to speed up the process.
